source: IISER IAT 2018 question paper (English, scanned), iiseradmission.in
_transcription: Scan with no text layer, transcribed from the page images. Chemistry = pages p04-p06 (printed page numbers 6-8) under the 'Chemistry' heading: printed Q16-Q22 on p04, Q23-Q27 on p05, Q28-Q30 on p06 (rest of p06 blank apart from show-through). The paper numbers its 60 questions straight through (Biology 1-15, Chemistry 16-30, ...), so ref/questionNumber restart at 1 here: printed Q16 = ref 1 ... printed Q30 = ref 15 (printed number = ref + 15). Printed numbers checked unbroken 16..30. Options are boxed A-D; where laid out in two columns (A, B left; C, D right) they are kept in A-D order. The faint mirror-image text from the back of each sheet was ignored. Drawn schemes: ref 6 (printed 21) starting material 4-methylaniline is drawn as a structure, typed by name with the scheme also cropped; its four options are X/Z structure pairs (picture options, typed as 'X = name and Z = name'). Ref 7 (22) and ref 10 (25) list drawn structures (i)-(iv), typed by name with the drawing cropped. Ref 8 (23) and ref 9 (24) schemes are fully typeable (acetone, drawn skeletally, typed as CH3COCH3), so not cropped. No answer key.

rows.text:
Select the correct order of basicity for the following compounds.

(i) piperidine

(ii) pyridine

(iii) pyrrolidin-2-one

(iv) diphenylamine

figure.note: Four skeletal structures labelled (i)-(iv): (i) saturated six-membered ring with N-H (piperidine); (ii) six-membered aromatic ring with N (pyridine); (iii) five-membered ring with N-H and C=O on the carbon next to N (pyrrolidin-2-one); (iv) two benzene rings joined through an N-H (diphenylamine).

Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their rate of reaction towards hydroxyl ion (\(\mathrm{OH^-}\)).

(i) 2-chloro-1,3,5-trinitrobenzene

(ii) 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene

(iii) 1-chloro-3-nitrobenzene

(iv) 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene

figure.note: Four benzene rings each with Cl at the top, labelled (i)-(iv): (i) NO2 on both carbons next to C-Cl and on the carbon opposite it; (ii) one NO2 next to C-Cl (ortho); (iii) one NO2 meta to Cl; (iv) one NO2 opposite Cl (para).

rows.subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
rows.text: The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons ejected from a metal on irradiation with light of frequency \(3.8 \times 10^{16}\) Hz is \(K\). When irradiated with light of frequency \(2.4 \times 10^{16}\) Hz, the kinetic energy of the photoelectrons becomes \(K/2\). What is the threshold frequency (\(\nu_0\)) of the metal?

rows.subtopic: Enthalpies for Different Types of Reactions
rows.text:
The heat of neutralization of the following reaction is \(-57.1\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\).

\(\mathrm{NaOH\ (aq) + HCl\ (aq) \rightarrow NaCl\ (aq) + H_2O\ (l)}\)

Which one of the following processes is mainly responsible for the heat released?

At 25 \(^\circ\)C, the standard reduction potential for the half-cell reaction

\(\mathrm{Zn\ (s) + 2H^+\ (aq) \rightarrow Zn^{2+}\ (aq) + H_2\ (g)}\)

is 0.28 V. What is the reduction potential of the half-cell reaction in 10M \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\) concentration, assuming all other species to be at unit concentration? [Universal gas constant, \(R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}\); Faraday constant, \(F = 96500\ \mathrm{C\ mol^{-1}}\)]
rows._flag: As printed: the equation the stem calls a 'half-cell reaction' is a whole cell reaction (Zn + 2H+ -> Zn2+ + H2), and it is given a 'standard reduction potential' of 0.28 V. Transcribed unchanged.

rows.text: In a cubic-close packed structure containing **X**, **Y** and **Z** atoms, if **Z** occupies all the face centers, **X** occupies all the corners and **Y** occupies the body center of the cube, what is the formula of this compound?

At 298 K, the vapour pressure of an ideal solution containing 1 mol of liquid **L1** and 2 mol of liquid **L2** is 500 mm Hg. When 2 mol of **L1** is added to this solution, the vapour pressure of the solution increases by 5%. What are the respective vapour pressures (in mm Hg) of **L1** and **L2** in their pure states at 298 K?
